result.title: Towards Human-AI Complementarity for AI Safety
result.summary: Safely overseeing AI is increasingly challenging for the humans doing it, as they must evaluate longer and more complex outputs with every new model generation. To mitigate this challenge, we could leverage complementarity: where humans and models make different mistakes, combining their judgements could yield an oversight signal stronger than either produces alone. We study this opportunity in realistic, safety-relevant settings, contributing the largest known suite of such tasks (3,957 instances across 8 datasets and 6 domains) as well as a platform and data pipeline for measuring human, AI, and human-AI performance on matched items. We collected 35,613 judgements from 416 human raters, finding a considerable opportunity for a complementarity effect. We also found that with the assistance methods we tested, human raters corrected the AI's errors less often, even when overall human accuracy rose, and the hybridisation methods we tested added little over the better single source on average. While complementarity is an important and feasible engineering target for safe oversight, achieving it remains an open challenge for future work.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建了面向安全监督的大规模人机协作评测资源（8 个数据集、6 个领域、3,957 条实例，并收集 416 名标注者共 35,613 条判断），用于匹配比较人类、AI 以及人机混合的监督准确率；结果显示互补性存在空间，但所测试的辅助与混合方法平均收益有限，甚至在人类整体更准时反而更少纠正 AI 的错误。
AI.relevance_reason: 属较远的 AI 安全监督领域，但其「互补性」度量与人机判断融合实验，可能为 LVR 中何时引入额外证据或计算（LOOK/STOP 的收益判断）提供评价思路，可供核查。
